spatial_claims.claim: M is the foot of the perpendicular from center N to chord BC, lying on BC with BM = MC = p/2
G lies on the circle on the minor arc BC, on the line NM extended; G is the midpoint of minor arc BC
Arc BG = arc GC = 1/10 of circle, so BG = GC = d (decagon side)
Vertex E is the midpoint of the major arc BC (at 2/5 from B along the major arc spanning 4/5); E is diametrically opposite G, making GE a diameter
G, N, M, E are collinear on the perpendicular to BC through N, with M between G and E
Angle GBE is a right angle (inscribed in semicircle on diameter GE)
Triangle GBE is right-angled at B; BE is a diagonal of the pentagon subtending 2/5 of the circle
Chords GE and BC intersect at M; by intersecting chords theorem GM * ME = BM * MC = (p/2)^2
Triangle GMB is right-angled at M (since GM perpendicular to BC at M)
Triangle EMB is right-angled at M (since EM perpendicular to BC at M)

configuration_map: Circle with center N, radius r. Pentagon ABCDE inscribed with vertices equally spaced (each arc = 1/5 of circle). M is the midpoint of chord BC (foot of perpendicular from N). G is the midpoint of minor arc BC (on the circle, collinear with N and M). E (pentagon vertex) is the midpoint of major arc BC, diametrically opposite G. Thus GE is a diameter passing through N and M, perpendicular to BC at M. The collinear order on line GE is G, M, N, E. Triangle GBE is right-angled at B (Thales). BM is the altitude from B to hypotenuse GE in this right triangle, creating two sub-right-triangles GMB and EMB (both right-angled at M). The intersecting chords GE and BC meet at M.
pass_reason: All spatial claims are mutually consistent. The identification of E as diametrically opposite G is valid (midpoints of complementary arcs). The collinearity G-M-N-E follows from the perpendicular from center to chord passing through both arc midpoints. The three right angles (at B in triangle GBE from Thales, at M in triangles GMB and EMB from the perpendicularity) are compatible: BM is the altitude from the right-angle vertex B to hypotenuse GE. The intersecting chords theorem at M is correctly applied. The algebraic derivation in Steps 12-17 follows validly from the geometric identities established in Steps 1-11, and the final result p^2 = r^2 + d^2 is numerically verified.
